newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end firm ahead of key industrial output data.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end firm ahead of key industrial output data.

text.p: Key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures closed firmer on Thursday on light buying from regional investors after Wednesday's sell-offs on the stronger-than-expected results of Bank of Japan's (BOJ) "tankan" survey of corporate sentiment.

Traders said the downside was solid as dealers had gone mostly long, hoping that major institutional investors may start buying on dips after Friday's May industrial output data, which is expected to be strong.
Another support was late falls in Tokyo stocks, with the key Nikkei index ending down 54.51 points at 20,624.76.
The key September contract closed up 0.22 at 123.27. It moved between 123.03 and 123.35 after opening at 123.15.
"Today's recovery was mainly led by short-covering from those who oversold yesterday," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit.
Such short-covering by dealers was prompted by scattered buy orders in cash bonds by regional investors, which started to appear this morning, following Wednesday's falls, he said.
Also, public funds were seen to have bought long-term cash JGBs in the afternoon, traders said.
The yield of the key 182nd 10-year JGB stood at 2.465 percent at 0653 GMT, down 0.015 from Wednesday's close.

"Before the tankan, there was a consensus that the BOJ would not change interest rates by the end of this year. But after the strong tankan results, that was corrected slightly. It now seems that a rate rise is possible after September only if economic data in the July-September period reflects a firm recovery," said a dealer at another bank's securities unit.
A senior BOJ official told Reuters late on Wednesday: "I don't think we can say that the economic recovery has become as strong as the improvement in the major manufacturers' DI."

The closely watched tankan showed that the diffusion index (DI) for major manufacturers rose to plus seven in June from plus two in March. But the DI for small non-manufacturers slipped to minus 11 from minus nine.

Market interest has now shifted to investors' attitudes after Friday's releases of key economic data, including May jobs data, Tokyo consumer price data for May and industrial output data for May and forecasts for June and July.
Economists polled this week by Reuters forecast increases ranging from 1.2 percent to 3.0 percent in May output, compared with a revised month-on-month drop of 0.5 percent in April.

"There are many domestic investors who haven't bought much in the past months. Given the strong tankan, most of them are now waiting for the industrial output data tomorrow as a clue to whether to increase or cut their bond holdings," said the second dealer.
Traders said the September may possibly fall to a recent low of 122.62 if the industrial production data, due at 1.30 p.m. (0430 GMT), is much stronger than expected.
A speech by BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita is also scheduled from 0040 p.m. (0340 GMT) on Friday.
